title: Procore Acquires DroneDeploy for $845M
summary: Procore Technologies announced on July 31, 2026 that it is acquiring DroneDeploy for $845 million in cash, structured as an asset acquisition and expected to close later in 2026 subject to regulatory approval. DroneDeploy runs a robotics and visual-intelligence platform for construction sites, capturing reality through drones, ground robots and mobile, fixed and wearable cameras, then using it for automated inspection and issue detection. Its platform has been used on more than 3 million job sites across over 180 countries, holds roughly 20 trillion square feet of visual data, and has catalogued more than 100,000 labelled safety issues. Procore CEO Ajei Gopal said the deal accelerates the company's AI strategy and its push to deliver 'digital co-workers' that track a project, interpret what they see and act on it — combining DroneDeploy's visual corpus with Procore's nearly 400 million photos and 126 million-plus drawings.
whyItMatters: This is a data acquisition wearing an M&A suit. Construction is the largest industry with almost no structured record of what physically happened on site, and 20 trillion square feet of captured reality plus 100,000 labelled safety issues is a training set no one can assemble from scratch. Paying $845 million for the corpus and the fleet that keeps refreshing it is a bet that the value in jobsite robotics sits in the perception layer and the labels, not in the drones — and it puts a market price on that view.
